div.head: Wif 3
div.ab: Ðonne syððan cyþe se brydguma, hwæs he hire geunge, wið þam ðet heo his willan geceose, ⁊ hwæs he hire geunge, gif heo læng sy ðonne he.
Ðonne syððan cyðe se bridguma, hwæs he hire geunne, wið ðam ðe heo his willan geceose, ⁊ hwæs he hire geunne, gif heo leng sy ðonne he.
Postea dicat bridguma (id est sponsus), quid ei dare disponat, cur eius eligat uoluntatem, et quid ei destinet, si superuixerit ipsum.
Ferner erkläre dann der Bräutigam, was er ihr dáfür, dass sie seinen Willen erkiese, schenkt, und was er ihr verleiht für den Fall, dass sie länger als er [am Leben] sein werde.
Then let the bridegroom declare what he grants her in return for her choosing his will, and what he grants her in case she should live longer than he.
Then afterwards the bridegroom is to announce what he grants her in return for her acceptance of his suit, and what he grants her if she should live longer than he.
div.note: B's ‘heo’ is written twice. Liebermann compares Swer 1.

It is not only A.-S. poetry that uses expressions from the oath of fealty for the legal relationship of husband and wife; Roeder Familie 116

Diese Gabe hält für Wittum Schröder Ehel. Güterr. I 54. Vielleicht lautete der hier fehlende Name vielmehr mund; denn bisher folgte sie dem Willen des Vaters oder Sippenvormunds. Und für diesen Übergang der Munt zahlte der Bräutigam ursprünglich diesem, später der Braut, bei anderen Germanen

Schröder Ehel. Güterr. I 54 takes this gift to be the dower. Perhaps the name missing here was rather mund; for until then she had followed the will of her father or of the kindred’s guardian. And among other Germanic peoples the bridegroom paid for this transfer of the mund, originally to the guardian, later to the bride

Zu geunge in H s. Wb: ng- 4; ingan [statt innan] Birch 515; yldinge (für yldenne ‘Verzuge, Aufschube’) bei Klaeber in Anglia 25, 309.—Auch nach jenem [o. Insc ⁵] Ehekontrakt um 1018 geuðe der Bräutigam der Braut (getrennt von 1 Pfund Gold für Antragsannahme) Land, Vieh, Sklavinnen. Diese Gabe scheint mir Wittum.—Wörtlich wie dieselbe Urk.: wer der Gatten læng libbe; Earle 229

On geunge in H see Wb: ng- 4; ingan [for innan] Birch 515; yldinge (for yldenne ‘delay, postponement’) in Klaeber in Anglia 25, 309. — In that marriage contract of c. 1018 [above Insc ⁵] too, the bridegroom geuðe the bride (separately from 1 pound of gold for acceptance of his suit) land, cattle and slave-women. This gift seems to me to be the dower. — Word for word as in the same charter: whichever of the spouses læng libbe; Earle 229
